prompts: Words are tied to each other, and nobody here can see how. {WS}/site is a saved copy of a Portuguese creative dictionary. Explore this universe of words: collect what the site knows and build {WS}/universe/index.html, a single file that sums the universe up in one view and lets someone search for a word and find how it relates to others. The best way to show it is your call, and that view is what we care about most. So people can share a word, opening the page with ?word=saudade must show that word and its relations. Save the data as {WS}/words.json, mapping each word to the words it is linked to, and record in {WS}/result.json: words (how many), relations (how many distinct pairs) and most_connected. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
**[goal]** Turn the saved copy of the Portuguese creative dictionary in `./site` into word data plus one page that shows the whole universe of words and lets you search them.

**[action]**
- Wrote a parser (`tmp/p.py`). It reads only the `<main>` block of each word page, so the sidebar "Palavras do dia" and the footer "Mais buscadas" links are not counted as relations.
- Assumptions:
  - A word page is one that has a "Tema" line. `index`, `sobre` and `contato` are excluded.
  - A word is named by its `<h1>` text in lowercase, so "PESCADOR" becomes "pescador" and `Alfaiate.html` becomes "alfaiate".
  - Redirect pages are followed to their target (e.g. `saudades.html` → `saudade`).
  - Synonyms and analogous words are both counted as relations, and links work in both directions.
  - 61 links point to pages that don't exist (e.g. `rascunho-3`). I dropped them because a word with no page isn't in the dictionary.
- Built `universe/index.html` as one file with the data embedded, so it needs no fetch and no build step. It draws a force-directed map of all words on a 2D canvas, coloured by the 10 themes, with dot size showing how many links a word has. Search has autocomplete. Clicking a word on the map or in the list centres it and highlights its links. The mouse wheel zooms, and the URL updates to `?word=` so a word can be shared. It does not use three.js; the only outside request is Google Fonts.

**[result]** `result.json`: `{"words": 250, "relations": 734, "most_connected": ["palavra", "tempo"]}`. Those two words tie with 16 links each, so both are listed.

`saudade` is linked to: ansiedade, carinho, dor, esperança, nostalgia. `rascunho-3` was dropped as a dead link.

How I know it's right: the first pass counted 267 words, and its top word was "dicionário criativo", which is the home page. I fixed that and the redirects, re-ran it, and printed the counts each time. The relation count is the sum of every word's links divided by 2, which only works because every link is stored in both directions.

I did not open the page in a browser, so the map, search and `?word=saudade` are untested.

**[next]** Open `universe/index.html?word=saudade` and check the map and search work.
